headline: High: gpt-researcher’s browser/API egress can amplify Airbyte-fed content into unsafe downstream actions; prompt-injection and leakage risks are otherwise moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can move business data through its API, and gpt-researcher explicitly uses browsers, MCP, and file inputs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Airbyte-fed documents are later consumed by gpt-researcher. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into gpt-researcher inputs or MCP tools
IF gpt-researcher treats retrieved file/web content as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP tools for the research run
Keep Airbyte outputs in a separate folder from research inputs
Add a manual prompt-injection review step before ingestion
Use read-only exports instead of live syncs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Airbyte and gpt-researcher

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data; gpt-researcher reads local files and sends queries/reports through third-party APIs. If Airbyte-produced data is placed into gpt-researcher’s workspace, that data can be uploaded onward. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is stored in gpt-researcher-readable files
IF gpt-researcher sends those files or derived notes to OpenAI/Tavily/LangChain/Gemini
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to synthetic or redacted inputs
Separate workspaces and mount Airbyte exports read-only
Turn off file ingestion for sensitive runs
Review outbound API destinations before execution
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on gpt-researcher uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and use MCP. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources and shared artifacts, so concurrent use can create write/overwrite conflicts even without a shared filesystem being explicitly documented. Uncertainty about orchestration pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or export directory
IF gpt-researcher writes reports while Airbyte refreshes synced artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Use file locks on exported reports
Make Airbyte destinations append-only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher flow can treat upstream material as research evidence, while Airbyte can supply business data through API-driven pipelines. If Airbyte content is wrong or manipulated, gpt-researcher may propagate it into reports or actions without strong verification. That downstream amplification makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests incorrect or attacker-controlled records
IF gpt-researcher publishes or acts on those records without independent verification
mitigations: Require source verification before publication
Add a human approval step for final reports
Cross-check Airbyte outputs against a second source
Limit gpt-researcher to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement citation provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple third-party APIs with broad egress. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or DPA alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the pair could move regulated business content into external services, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into gpt-researcher
IF the external APIs used by gpt-researcher are not covered by the applicable DPA or residency policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to gpt-researcher
Block regulated datasets from external API calls
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings
Minimize retention of generated reports
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing controls
